strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor today. The long straights and high-speed corners of this 6.436km layout will punish the rubber.
The pit window is likely to open around lap 15, depending on tire wear and fuel consumption. A well-timed stop could be crucial.
Fuel management will be critical, especially in the closing stages. Drivers will need to balance speed with conservation.
An early safety car could throw the entire strategy out the window, forcing teams to react quickly and make tough decisions.
The long straights offer plenty of opportunities for slipstreaming and overtaking, so expect to see some strategic moves on track.
With such a long lap, getting caught behind slower traffic can be extremely costly, potentially ruining a driver's race.
The historic layout of Road America offers limited run-off in some areas, so safety car periods are common, influencing strategy.
Teams will be monitoring tire temperatures closely, as overheating can lead to a significant drop in performance on this demanding circuit.
weatherCommentary: The Wisconsin weather can be unpredictable. A sudden downpour could turn this race on its head.
The wind direction can play a significant role, affecting the car's balance at high speeds, especially through the Kink.
With the track temperature soaring, tire management will be even more crucial today. Drivers will need to be gentle on their rubber.
The humidity is high, which will make conditions even more challenging for the drivers inside the cockpit.
There's a chance of thunderstorms later this afternoon, which could lead to a dramatic conclusion to the race.
